title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. Ĝ is a profinite group with two distinguished elements ρ, σ, of orders 3 and 2 in the motivating cases. B_{ρ,σ} is a group of automorphisms of Ĝ adapted to (ρ,σ). L_0 ⊂ Ĝ is the subgroup of elements whose inner automorphism lies in B_{ρ,σ}.

Construction (pp. 504–505). Form the semidirect product S_0G = B ⋉ Ĝ. Divide by the normal subgroup i(L_0), where i(ℓ) = (int ℓ, ℓ^{-1}). This gives G_{ρ,σ} = S_0G / i(L_0). In it the inner automorphisms of elements of L_0 are identified with those elements themselves. It is the standard 'amalgamate Ĝ with a group of automorphisms along Inn' construction: the extension group attached to an outer action.

Kernel of Ĝ → G_{ρ,σ}. It equals L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ), which is also the kernel of L_0 → B.

This page:
(i) For Ĝ = SL(2,Ẑ)' this intersection is trivial. Grothendieck therefore proposes to assume in general (18): L_0 ∩ Centre(Ĝ) = 1. Then Ĝ injects into G_{ρ,σ}, and L_0 injects into B.
(ii) The image of L_0 → B, ℓ ↦ int(ℓ), is normal in B. Set Γ_{ρ,σ} = B / Im L_0.
(iii) Then G_{ρ,σ}/Ĝ ≅ B/L_0 ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ}. The marginal note (20 bis) records this as a nine-lemma diagram of two exact rows:
- 1 → L_0 → B → Γ → 1,
- 1 → Ĝ → G → Γ → 1,
with vertical maps L_0 → Ĝ and B → G.
So G_{ρ,σ} is the pushout of B along L_0 → Ĝ. It is the 'arithmetic' extension of the 'Galois-type' quotient Γ by the 'geometric' group Ĝ.

NB, worked toy example: Ĝ = SL(2,Ẑ)'.
- B_{ρ,σ} ⊂ GP(Ẑ) (some projective-linear group over Ẑ) is the previously studied group B'_0.
- The hypothesis B'_0 = B_{ρ,σ} gives Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ G_m, i.e. Ẑ^*.
- This uses the splitting B'_0 = T_0 ⋉ L_0 with T_0 a torus, T_0 ≅ B'_0/L_0 ≅ G_m.
- Hence G_{ρ,σ} ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)'. The construction recovers GL_2 from SL_2, with the determinant (cyclotomic-like) quotient Ẑ^* playing the role of Γ.

The margin seems to say the case (SL(2,Ẑ)', ρ, σ) is thereby brought back to the case G = GL(2,Ẑ).

Purpose. The next page contrasts this with the 'universal' case Ĝ = profinite completion of the genus-0, 3-point Teichmüller-type group. There Γ_{ρ,σ} is a huge, non-commutative group containing the image of Gal(Q̄/Q). So the page is a toy-model calibration of an abstract 'Galois–Teichmüller' group Γ_{ρ,σ} built from loop-equation data, in the spirit of what became the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group.
errors: Equation number (18) is reused: it already labels the kernel formula on the previous page.
Notation drift: (19) defines Γ*_{ρ,σ} = B/Im L_0, but (20) writes B/L_0 ≅ Γ_{ρ,σ}. Writing B/L_0 is legitimate only under hypothesis (18), which makes L_0 → B injective.

Sign inconsistency carried over from the previous page: i(g) = int(g^{-1})·g^{-1} in (14) versus int(g)·g^{-1} in the verification. Harmless, as either choice gives a normal subgroup if used consistently.
The identification Γ ≅ G_m (Ẑ^*) and G_{ρ,σ} ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)' depends on unspecified meanings of the primes (SL', GL') and of GP(Ẑ). The index-2 / ±1 bookkeeping is not checked on the page.

ideas.what: Build the extension G = (B ⋉ Ĝ)/{(int ℓ, ℓ^{-1})} from a group B of automorphisms of Ĝ and the subgroup L_0 of elements whose inner automorphisms lie in B. Its kernel on Ĝ is the centre part L_0 ∩ Z(Ĝ).
ideas.modern_name: Extension associated with an outer action / pushout along Inn; holomorph-type amalgamation (as in the fundamental exact sequence for arithmetic π_1 when the centre is trivial)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical group extension theory (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); used in SGA1-style anabelian settings
ideas.where_published: Implicit in SGA1 and the Longue Marche discussion of outer Galois actions; not as this explicit formula, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Normality of int(L_0) in B, and the nine-lemma diagram giving G/Ĝ ≅ B/L_0 = Γ_{ρ,σ}.

Toy model: for Ĝ = SL(2,Ẑ)' the abstract 'Galois-type' group Γ_{ρ,σ} is Ẑ^* (G_m). The resulting arithmetic extension is GL(2,Ẑ)', split by a torus T_0. This contrasts with the universal 0,3 case, where Γ contains the image of Gal(Q̄/Q).
ideas.modern_name: GL_2 / SL_2 with determinant as a cyclotomic-character analogue of Gal(Q̄/Q) → GT; Ẑ^* as abelianised shadow of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (pro-l Galois representations, 1980s); Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Lochak–Schneps for GT variants
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Teichmüller towers and Gal(Q̄/Q) acting on them, but not this explicit SL_2 → GL_2 calibration.

missed.claim: This is an explicit abstract definition of a 'Teichmüller–Galois' group Γ_{ρ,σ} = B_{ρ,σ}/Inn-part, attached to a profinite group with an order-2 and an order-3 element. It is calibrated on SL(2,Ẑ)' (giving Ẑ^* and GL(2,Ẑ)') before the universal case (giving a group containing Gal(Q̄/Q)'). It documents Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld approach to a GT-like group through the PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 presentation. Mathematically it is routine group theory; the historical interest is moderate.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians of GT and of anabelian geometry may want to document how Grothendieck set up an abstract 'Galois-type' group via automorphisms preserving (ρ,σ). This anticipates Drinfeld's ĜT, which is defined through the (λ, f) action on generators of order 2 and 3.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine group-extension bookkeeping plus a sanity check on SL_2 → GL_2. Its interest lies only in the surrounding project, a pre-Drinfeld GT-like construction, which is already broadly known to be among Grothendieck's ideas.
transcription_corrections: In (18), 'G ↪ A_{ρ,σ} inj.' most likely reads 'Ĝ ↪ G_{ρ,σ} inj.' (injectivity of Ĝ into G_{ρ,σ}).
First line, likely '(avec ρ, σ comme à l'ordinaire)'.
Left margin, likely 'i.e. lemme des neuf' or 'diagramme à 9 entrées', followed by (20 bis) with two exact rows. The vertical maps are L_0 ↪ Ĝ and B_{ρ,σ} ↪ G_{ρ,σ}, with Ĝ = SG_{ρ,σ}.
Bottom-left margin, likely: 'donc le cas (G = SL(2,Ẑ)', ρ, σ) se ramène au cas G = GL(2,Ẑ)...'.
'T_0 ⥲ B'_0/L_0 ≃ G_m': the subscript is T_0 (torus), not Γ_0, in the semidirect product B'_0 = T_0 · L_0.
